description: Composite three-panel figure whose panels are all true stress-true strain plots, each carrying an embedded row of DIC strain-field strips along the strain axis. (a) AN750-T: y-axis "True stress (MPa)" 0-1500 with ticks 0, 300, 600, 900, 1200, 1500; x-axis "True strain" with printed ticks 0.04, 0.08, 0.12, 0.16, 0.20. Legend: solid red "Experiment", dashed black "Iso-work model". The red experimental curve lies above the dashed iso-work model over the whole range and the widening gap between them is filled grey and labelled σ_B; the words "Stress relieving" are printed at the right; black circles in the DIC strips mark local strain-concentration points and black upward arrows mark their growth. (b) AN800-T: same y-axis, x ticks 0.01-0.07; the two curves cross and converge at high strain; annotation "Second local strain concentration" with a dashed ellipse, and diagonal arrows indicate the two concentration points spreading at ~45° and connecting. (c) AN850-T: x ticks 0.01-0.06; DIC strips show a broadened strain-concentration band with no text annotation. Together the panels demonstrate that the iso-work constitutive model increasingly underestimates true stress with strain, the gap being the back stress σ_B, and that strain localisation behaviour differs between AN750-T, AN800-T and AN850-T.

True stress (MPa, 0-1500) vs True strain (ticks 0.01-0.07) for AN800-T; 'Experiment' and 'Iso-work model' curves converge at higher strain; DIC strips with annotation 'Second local strain concentration' (dashed ellipse) and diagonal arrows showing ~45° spreading of two concentration points.

observations.observation: The figure is a three-panel composite in which every panel is a true stress-true strain plot with an inline row of colour DIC strain-field strips beneath the curves.

Panel (a) plots True stress (MPa) from 0 to 1500 (ticks 0, 300, 600, 900, 1200, 1500) against True strain with printed ticks 0.04, 0.08, 0.12, 0.16, 0.20; panels (b) and (c) use the same stress scale with strain ticks 0.01-0.07 and 0.01-0.06 respectively.
Both curves in every panel are identified by a legend with exactly two entries: solid red 'Experiment' and dashed black 'Iso-work model'.
The grey shaded area between the experimental curve and the iso-work model curve is labelled σ_B.
In panel (a) the experimental curve stays above the iso-work model curve and the grey band widens as true strain increases, with the words 'Stress relieving' printed near the right-hand end.
Panel (a) contains black circles over the DIC strips marking local strain-concentration points and black upward arrows marking their progression with strain.

Panel (b) is annotated 'Second local strain concentration' with a dashed ellipse, and diagonal arrows across the DIC strips indicate the two concentration points expanding at about 45 degrees and connecting.

The caption labels the three panels as true strain curves for (a) AN750-T, (b) AN800-T and (c) AN850-T, and describes the figure as the constitutive relationship fitting curve and experimental data comparison of these three samples.

The caption states the plot y-axes are true strain and the citing text states the insets are DIC strain fields; the insets themselves carry no readable colour bar or numeric strain scale in the supplied rendering.
The citing text reports that the maximum stress caused by σ_B at the necking strain was 217, 300 and 278 MPa for AN750-T, AN800-T and AN850-T respectively.
The citing text states that the difference between the constitutive model prediction and the experimentally obtained mechanical performance curve gradually increases as true strain increases.

The citing text states the AN750-T sample exhibits relatively uniform strain during the yield stage and a stress-distribution phenomenon during uniform plastic deformation, marked by a circle in Fig. 9(a).
The citing text states that in the AN800-T sample two local strain concentration points appear, expand at a 45° angle and connect, leading to necking.

The citing text attributes the more pronounced strain distribution in AN750-T to strain-hardening behaviour induced by TRIP during deformation, while noting similar behaviour in AN800-T and AN850-T with lower RA content.
